| `geometry/item_display_transforms` | partial | The eight context names, the units and the three fields are the same in both editions, so the mapping is the identity and the only work is the axis conversion — which is the model's own, applied to a displacement rather than to a position. The ORDER the three angles compose in is not observed. Java's half is read off the jar - the transform is applied as rotationXYZ, so X then Y then Z - and Bedrock is assumed to match. The mirror preserves whatever the order is, so a transform turning about one axis is right either way; only one turning about two at once could show a difference. What Bedrock does for the LEFT HAND is not observed either. Java mirrors its two left-hand contexts itself at render time, whether or not the model declares one, so a pack's left-hand values are passed through verbatim: right if Bedrock inherited that convention with the rest of the system, and mirrored in the off hand if it did not. A context the pack does not state is not written, which leaves minecraft:block/block answering for it. That is Java's per-context inheritance rather than Bedrock's defaults, and the two have not been compared. |
